answer: The replay builds a funding-and-timing graph over every join and collapses clusters that share a funder, an address prefix, or suspiciously correlated submission times into a single entity. The falcon report reveals the merge explicitly at each ripple. Because of that, an attacker who spins up 231 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 99 times the capital for one share. That is 20 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
